notes:
DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the family-config / SerialDriver shape was replaced by a direct Driver with a native.py factory. The upstream is a Qt main window whose button handlers each open COM1, write one line and close it (pumpcontroller.py:228-389); a run is the pair 'set the rate' and RUN, and the safe state is the three lines STP, 01STP and 02STP, which a one-line-per-capability command table cannot express. The driver still writes exactly the clone's bytes and calls the upstream handler names through the fake or the injected-port hardware object. No command syntax was changed.

Covered on the fake backend only: G1-G9 passed with no findings and no warnings. No hardware was attached; the hardware backend was never imported or run. The package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null).

The fake is a recording stand-in, not a transcript: the clone contains no recorded exchange and the protocol is write-only (the upstream never reads a reply, pumpcontroller.py:232-235), so there is nothing to replay. Its starting values and empty line-edit texts are placeholders, not facts. The reads flow_rate, diameter and pumping report the last values this driver commanded, not measurements; the pump's own state is never queried. The driver exposes address 00 by default (the unprefixed handler group) and addresses 01 and 02 through the 'address' option; the upstream's three pump groups are otherwise unchanged. The ULH and ULM flow-rate commands are not exposed (the driver uses MLH in mL/h), so the upstream's 02ULM copy-paste defect (pumpcontroller.py:355-358) is not used. No volume, position or reply-based completion is covered: the clone has none, and the driver does not invent one.

Limits: no text file of the clone states a flow-rate or diameter range, so both numeric writes are Limit.operator_required. site-limits.example.json carries example operator bounds for the acceptance run only; those numbers are not device facts and are not copied into driver.py. Without an operator overlay every write is refused MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET. The driver is R2 because the pump dispenses liquid (MHS/spec/04-safety.md), above the card's R0 floor; the safe-state action x-cap.drkirkm.stop.v1 is the independent stop path, and the native e-stop sends the stop handler of the configured address. The clone states no independent hardware e-stop, so no estop_physical_ref is claimed.

Not covered: the wire format of the flow-rate and diameter numbers (Python's g format, e.g. 12.06) was not checked against a pump; the upstream passes whatever text a user typed. The hardware backend needs pyserial (README.md:5) and a serial port option (the clone hardcodes COM1, README.md:6); nothing here ran it.
